dismissed.why_not_material: Filed 2025-11-10, states 'enrollment is ongoing'. The refutation is based on cutoff status 2026-03-24 showing ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING as of 2026-02-25. The claim predates the enrollment completion by 3+ months; this is a temporal mismatch, not masking of known bad news at time of claim.

Timeline guidance inconsistency (Q4 2026 vs registered October 2026) is a minor restatement. October is early Q4; the slip from 2025-10 to 2026-10 was publicly registered in August 2024. The May 2026 claim maintains Q4 2026, which encompasses the registered October date. This is not masking a miss.

Same as cldx_002: the February 2026 claim of 'Q4 2026' is consistent with the registered 2026-10 primary completion (October is Q4). The registered slip occurred in August 2024, well before this claim. No masking of the catalyst trial timeline.

This is standard early-stage promotion. The 'best-in-disease' claim is based on cross-trial benchmarking of conference presentations, not a misrepresentation of the catalyst Phase 3 trial design or results. The Phase 3 NCT06455202 is properly registered as placebo-controlled; claiming potential leadership based on Phase 2 data is normal IR, per principle #3.

Same as cldx_005: 'best-in-disease' claims from Phase 2 CSU data presented at medical meetings. The catalyst is a Phase 3 placebo-controlled RCT. Touting earlier-phase data alongside a pivotal trial is supporting color, not masking of the Phase 3 design or expected performance.

Same rationale as cldx_005 and cldx_009: Phase 2 'best in disease' claim from August 2025. This is promotional language about earlier data, not a misrepresentation of the catalyst Phase 3 trial's basis or results.

Filed May 2025, claims 'best-in-class efficacy' based on Phase 2 chronic urticaria data. This is normal biotech promotion of uncontrolled early data. The Phase 3 catalyst trial is properly designed as placebo-controlled RCT; no masking of that trial's design or interim results.

Filed February 2025, references 'best-in-disease data' from Phase 2 CSU and CIndU studies in 2024. Standard promotional language about earlier-phase results. Does not misrepresent the catalyst Phase 3 trial design, which is transparently placebo-controlled.

Filed February 2025, cites 71% complete response at Week 52 in Phase 2 (150mg Q4W) as 'highest rate observed in a well controlled study'. This is a cross-trial benchmark of Phase 2 data, not a claim about the catalyst Phase 3 trial. Normal early-stage IR, per principle #3.

analyst_note: All nine refuted findings are minor severity and fall into two categories: timeline/enrollment status claims that predate material changes (cldx_016, cldx_002, cldx_012), and cross-trial 'best-in-disease' promotional language based on Phase 2 data (cldx_005, cldx_009, cldx_043, cldx_050, cldx_052, cldx_054). The timeline claims reflect normal lag between marketing and registry updates, not masking of a known miss. The efficacy overreach claims are standard biotech promotion of earlier-phase uncontrolled data alongside a properly registered Phase 3 placebo-controlled RCT (NCT06455202). No company-level honesty red flags, no manipulation of the catalyst trial's design or endpoints, and no material masking detected. This setup is consistent with an honest sponsor going into a blind readout.
